gaps.sentence: ___ of my friends knew about the concert, so I went on my own.
gaps.explanation: 'None of my friends' means zero friends; 'no' cannot stand before 'of' and 'nothing' is not a quantifier here.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ enthusiasm for the proposal, so it was quietly shelved.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' (without 'a') means not enough — which explains shelving the proposal.

gaps.sentence: ___ the food was eaten within minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'All the food' is correct with an uncountable noun; 'whole' needs 'the whole of' and 'both' needs two separate items.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ in a bad mood.
gaps.explanation: 'Mostly' is an adverb meaning mainly or usually; 'most' as a quantifier needs a noun.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.

gaps.sentence: There are ___ than forty applicants for every training place.
gaps.explanation: 'More than' + number expresses quantities above a figure.

gaps.sentence: Try to eat ___ sugar and more vegetables.
gaps.explanation: 'Less' is the comparative for uncountable nouns like sugar; 'fewer' is for countables.

gaps.sentence: The twins are ___ over six feet tall.
gaps.explanation: 'Both' is used for exactly two; 'all' is for three or more.
